issue_context.title: CRYPTO_THREAD_read_lock() and CRYPTO_THREAD_write_lock() can fail
issue_context.body: It is possible for `CRYPTO_THREAD_read_lock()` and  `CRYPTO_THREAD_write_lock()` to fail. For example if `PTHREAD_MUTEX_ERRORCHECK` is in use and we hit a deadlock then they will fail. Unfortunately while we do check for failure in some locations there are many locations where we do not. This means we carry on regardless assuming we have successfully obtained the lock even though we haven't. (See also issue #14229)
comments:
The return value from these looks to be ignored more often than not 😞 

Is it viable to tag them `__owur`?
In theory the unlock function could fail as well.

> In theory the unlock function could fail as well.

I would rather see this as a separate issue.  If you can't lock, you can at least fail the operation and report back. If you can't unlock, what should you do?  (And a future lock will fail anyway)

No. At least not in the pthreads implementation.
Well..at least there are some codepaths that call assert on failure but not others.
I think it makes sense to put ossl_assert into the locking calls.  What do you think?

The question is whether they could ever fail for reasons other than a programming error. If they can then assert is probably not appropriate. If not then it probably is. If the only reason that a locking call will ever fail is because of a programming error then I see no reason not to put the asserts in the locking calls themselves.
locking can fail because of lack of system resources. It is unlikely, but possible, just like malloc failing on other than embedded systems.
Should it raise an error?
